content.text:
**Legally, under international law and the position of most countries: no — Crimea does not belong to Russia; it is recognized as part of Ukraine.** The UN General Assembly affirmed Ukraine’s territorial integrity in March 2014 and called the Crimea referendum invalid, urging states not to recognize any change in Crimea’s status. ([press.un.org](https://press.un.org/en/2014/ga11493.doc.htm?utm_source=openai))

**Practically, Russia has controlled Crimea since 2014** after occupying and annexing it, and Russia treats Crimea as part of the Russian Federation. But that annexation is not recognized by Ukraine, the United States, the EU, and most UN member states. The U.S. position, for example, is that it “does not, and will never, recognize” Russia’s annexation of Crimea. ([2021-2025.state.gov](https://2021-2025.state.gov/crimea-is-ukraine/?utm_source=openai))

So the short answer is:

- **De jure / legally:** Crimea is Ukrainian territory.  
- **De facto / on the ground:** Crimea is controlled by Russia.
